chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Sufyan, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, who said:

Ibn al-Kawa' said to Ali (peace be upon him): O Commander of the Faithful, what do you make of your saying: 'The wonder is between Jumada and Rajab'? He (peace be upon him) said: Woe to you, O One-Eyed! It is the gathering of scattered things, the raising of the dead, the harvesting of vegetation, and calamities upon calamities, destroying and annihilating; neither I nor you will be there.

key_terms.أَعْوَرَ: Al-A'war (The One-Eyed, a nickname for Ibn al-Kawa')

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Imam Ali's saying 'The wonder is between Jumada and Rajab'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates his enigmatic phrase 'The wonder is between Jumada and Rajab' as a period of intense cosmic and earthly upheaval characterized by the gathering of scattered resources, resurrection of the dead, and successive calamities. This interpretation highlights the transient nature of worldly power and life, emphasizing that both the Imam and his interlocutor, Ibn al-Kawa', will perish during this era of destruction, underscoring the inevitability of divine decree and the temporary nature of human existence.
